description: Catch up: everything a person or group did, and where they were named, in a window, newest first per kind (mail grouped by thread). who: a name (fuzzy; close matches return ambiguous [{name, hash}]), email, hash:<8 hex>, team:<slug>, org:<name>, new:<window>, a phrase ('the core team'), or a list. since/until: ISO date, today, 2w/14d/1m, pg19 (a release's development window), all; default 14 days. during: a calendar event uid/url. topic narrows by hybrid search. Kinds: waiting (one person, no topic: what is on their radar, each with its rule (reply_to_you > called_out > to_cc > named, then commitfest and cfbot rules, then code_changed: open patches changing files they wrote much of on master in threads they have not posted in, group code_changes, with files and their share, score, proposer, patch_url; called_out items carry call_out {evidence, excerpt, confidence, url} quoting the message that asked them to take part), group, priority 0-100 and why, and an outlook (a model's estimate: unit commitfest = P(commit) for the CF and release and thread health, when its thread is in an open commitfest; unit thread = p_commit, P(a commit from a patch thread in no commitfest within horizon_days); people to seek out, factors, model_version)), acted (one person, no topic: what they did about what waited on them: answered, sent_patch, committed, with what asked them and when; an item leaves waiting when they act and shows here), mail_from, mail_to_cc, mail_mention, git_author, git_credit, git_mention, wiki_edit, wiki_mention, commitfest, calendar, roster. Names, page hashes and urls only, never addresses. ~4 s budget; late kinds go in timed_out with partial=true. Cite each item's url. Same as GET /api/v2/activity.

during.description: A calendar event uid or url, or pg19: sets since and until to its dates

since.description: Window start: 2026-10-01, 2w, 14d, 1m, today, pg19, all (default 14 days ago)

topic.description: Optional topic that narrows every kind, e.g. NUMA, benchmarking

who.description: Who: 'Tom Lane', 'team:core-team', 'org:Amazon/AWS', 'new:30d', a 8-hex person hash, an email; a string or a list of strings

name: whats_new
